s: Lakeshore Inn is preparing for its busiest weekend, a regional rowing regatta. Last year the hotel received complaints about long check-in lines, room mix-ups and staff who seemed rushed and unhelpful.

The general manager (judge) is interviewing candidates for front desk agent. She wants you to explain what great guest relations looks like at a hotel, how you would handle a guest who arrives to find their room is not ready, and how front desk employees shape the hotel's image.
p: Explain the nature of positive customer relations
Handle difficult customers
Respond to customer inquiries
Determine ways of reinforcing the company's image through employee performance

Stays calm with an upset guest, apologizes, explains options and offers a fix (upgrade, lounge, luggage storage)
Answers questions accurately or finds out and follows up
Explains that each employee interaction is the hotel's brand
q: A guest says, 'I booked six months ago and I want the room I reserved.' It is not available. What do you say?
How would you handle a guest who is rude to you in front of other guests?

c: Summit Peaks Tourism Board, which promotes a mountain resort region
s: Tourism in the Summit Peaks region fell sharply two winters ago after a poor snow season and rose again last year when airfares dropped. Local hotels and restaurants say their income swings with the weather and the economy.
The executive director (judge) wants you to explain why tourism is affected by supply and demand and the business cycle, and how a destination can lower its risk of depending on a single season.
p: Explain the principles of supply and demand
Determine the impact of business cycles on business activities
Determine factors affecting business risk
Identify the impact of small business/entrepreneurship on market economies

Describes how prices change in peak and off-peak seasons
Names weather, fuel prices, exchange rates and competition as risk factors
Suggests diversifying with summer activities, events and local small businesses
q: Why do hotel rates rise when a big festival is in town?
What would you do to attract visitors during the slowest months?

c: Orchid Garden Resort, a 200-room beachfront resort
s: Orchid Garden Resort recently had a fire alarm during dinner service. Guests were unsure where to go, one guest slipped on the stairs, and staff were not sure who was in charge.

Explain routine security precautions
Maintain data security

Key control, lighting, ID checks and not announcing room numbers aloud
Secure payment systems, limited access to records and staff training
q: A guest asks you for another guest's room number. What do you do?
How would you keep service going while following all safety rules in a crisis?

c: Brightwater Inn & Spa, a boutique hotel
s: Brightwater Inn & Spa is half empty on weeknights. The marketing director believes many business travelers and nearby residents do not know the hotel has a spa, a restaurant and a meeting room.

Buying factors: price, location, reviews, amenities, loyalty perks, convenience

Staff can suggest the spa, ask for reviews and share local tips
q: Which would matter more to a business traveler, price or location, and why?
What is one low-cost idea to fill rooms on a Tuesday night?

c: Pinecrest Lodge, a ski lodge with 90 rooms and a restaurant
